current.text: Dallas has very few true ball handlers. The only real guards are Kyrie Irving, rookie Sergio de Larrea and Marcus Sasser. Max Christie and Cooper Flagg are not point guards.

The frontcourt is crowded. Almost every player besides Irving is a power forward, and Dereck Lively II, Daniel Gafford, P.J. Washington, Santi Aldama, Naji Marshall and Morez Johnson Jr. all compete for frontcourt minutes.
The roster is overloaded with wings who expect minutes. It had 16 players in late July.
The deep frontcourt limits Santi Aldama's minutes.
Dusty May is the new head coach. How he will split the center minutes between Lively, Gafford, Powell and Johnson Jr., plus forwards like Washington and Aldama, is unknown.
Lively, Dharma and Morez Johnson Jr. are all hurt. That makes Gafford the likely opening night center.
Josh's projected starting five is Irving, Christie, Flagg, Washington and Morez Johnson Jr.
Cooper Flagg is the first option on offense. Irving is the second.
Irving's return will take shots mostly from players other than Flagg.
So many power forwards on the floor limits Flagg's chances to block shots.
Irving is 36 and coming off an injury, so the thin guard group has little cover behind him.
Dallas added shooting across the roster, including Santi Aldama and Sergio de Larrea.
Dallas is rebuilding on the fly around Flagg, and this is a fact-finding season.
Dallas could be a bad team. The Western Conference is weak, though, so a playoff push is possible. The market win total of 34.5 ranks 23rd of 30.
Dallas does not control its own first-round pick. It is owed to Charlotte with top-two protection.
Without its pick, Dallas has no reason to tank, so the risk of late-season tanking is low.
One more move is expected. Daniel Gafford and/or Klay Thompson could be traded.
Dallas has the best fantasy playoff schedule: 4 games in each of weeks 19, 20 and 21, for 12 games in total (rank 1 of 30). There is only one back-to-back pair across those weeks, in week 19.
Dallas has 16 back-to-backs, one of the highest totals in the league (rank 26 of 30). That raises rest risk for older or injury-prone players like Irving during the regular season.
Dallas plays only two games in the matchup week starting March 1, which is the week before our playoffs.
Josh sees no strong reason to fade Dallas players. He thinks most of their draft positions are reasonable.

durable.text: The front office cares little about positions. It collects talent to see who sticks, which leads to crowded position groups and unclear roles.

note: Dallas has the best playoff schedule in the league (4-4-4) and no reason to tank, which helps every Mav in weeks 19 to 21. Flagg and Irving lead the usage, and the thin guard group makes Irving, Sasser and de Larrea the only real ball handlers, but the frontcourt logjam caps Aldama, Washington and the centers. Early on, watch how new coach Dusty May splits center minutes while Lively and Johnson Jr. are hurt, and whether a Gafford trade happens.
